clue.text: Race tyres can burst

indicators.note: something burst is blown apart, so the letters of the two words before it are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: A warning that the tyres on a racing car might blow out.
explanation.definitionFit: A race in the sense of a people or line of descent is a synonym for lineage.

clue.text: Tiny changes to adopt church's point

indicators.note: to adopt is to take in, so the shuffled letters take the church abbreviation inside them
the word Tiny changes into a new order of its letters

parts.note: CE stands for Church of England

explanation.surface: A tiny alteration lets the church adopt a fine point of doctrine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tiny' reads as a description of the changes but is the fodder; 'changes' makes NITY, and 'to adopt' has it take in the church letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A nicety is a subtle distinction or fine detail, one sense of a point.

clue.text: Rescue former lover and Conservative wearing strange attire

parts.note: an ex is a former partner

indicators.note: the shuffled clothing word is worn around the party letter, holding it inside
strange signals that the letters of attire are put in an unusual order

explanation.surface: Saving an ex and a Tory politician who have turned up in odd clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wearing' sounds like clothing in the surface, but it is the container signal: the 'strange' shuffle of the outfit word, TRIATE, wraps round the party letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To extricate someone is to free them from a difficulty, a synonym of rescue as a verb.

clue.text: Sort of negativism characterised by speed and efficiency

indicators.note: to sort is to arrange, so the letters of the next word are sorted into another order

explanation.surface: A kind of negativism that is somehow quick and efficient.
explanation.definitionFit: Something time-saving gets jobs done quickly with little waste, the speed and efficiency described.

clue.text: Burden left for bumpkin

parts.note: a yoke is a heavy burden or oppressive load

explanation.surface: A heavy load left behind for a country fellow to carry.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean an unsophisticated person from the countryside.

clue.text: Cut piece, dry inside

indicators.note: inside places the word for dry within the word for piece

parts.note: a bit is a small piece
sec is the French word for dry, used of wine

explanation.surface: Instructions to cut a piece of something with dry stuff inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To bisect is to cut into two halves, a specific kind of cutting.

clue.text: No clothes are worn in this city

definitions.text: No clothes are worn in this city

parts.words: No clothes are worn in this city
parts.note: the city in Somerset shares its name with the tub in which people wash undressed

explanation.surface: A city where everyone apparently walks about naked.
explanation.walkthrough: BATH is a Roman spa city in the west of England; in a bath nobody wears clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: The English city and the washing tub share one name, so a place where clothing is shed fits both.

clue.text: Flight member's fixed gaze, one hears

indicators.note: one hears marks that the word is heard rather than read, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: a stare is a long fixed look

explanation.surface: A member of an aircraft crew fixing someone with a steady look.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flight' suggests aircraft, but here it means a flight of steps.
explanation.definitionFit: A single step is one member of a flight of steps.

clue.text: Dance with seal round a garden?

indicators.note: the sealing word goes round the next letters, enclosing them

parts.note: calk is a variant spelling of caulk, to seal seams
Kew is the famous botanic garden in London

explanation.surface: A seal performing a dance around a garden.
explanation.walkthrough: KEW Gardens is London's royal botanic garden; CALK is the less common spelling of caulk.
explanation.definitionFit: The cakewalk is a strutting dance that originated among African Americans in the nineteenth century.

clue.text: Northerner, no adult on course

indicators.note: no means the adult letter is left out of the course

parts.note: Ascot is a famous English racecourse
A is the film-rating abbreviation for adult

explanation.surface: A northerner, not yet grown up, out on a racecourse.
explanation.walkthrough: ASCOT is a racecourse in Berkshire, home of Royal Ascot.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Scotland comes from the north of Britain, so he is a northerner.

clue.text: Leave footprints and hurry

definitions.meaning: taken literally, the phrase means to leave marks behind as one walks
the idiom means to leave quickly

explanation.surface: Someone walking quickly and leaving prints behind.
explanation.walkthrough: The literal reading, making tracks in mud, sits beside the idiom for departing in haste.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to set off or depart quickly, and literally to produce footprints.

clue.text: Greek sailor's dry wit

parts.note: Attic means of Attica or Athens, hence Greek
an old salt is a seasoned sailor

explanation.surface: A Greek seaman known for his deadpan humour.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names refined, understated humour like that credited to ancient Athenians, so dry wit is a synonym.

clue.text: Priest to have gloomy expression

parts.note: Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest's title
to own is to have or possess

explanation.surface: A priest who is supposed to wear a glum face.
explanation.definitionFit: A scowling look of displeasure or worry is a gloomy expression on the face.

clue.text: Host who knows all the answers

definitions.text: Host who knows all the answers

parts.words: Host who knows all the answers
parts.note: suggests a know-all, but means the presenter of a quiz who holds the answer cards

explanation.surface: A host who is an insufferable know-it-all.
explanation.definitionFit: The presenter of a quiz show holds every correct answer in advance, so knows them all.

clue.text: Might sculptor be found sitting in it?

definitions.text: Might sculptor be found sitting in it?

parts.words: Might sculptor be found sitting in it?
parts.note: the word for one who carves wood or stone is also a type of dining chair with arms

explanation.surface: A puzzle about where a sculptor likes to sit.
explanation.walkthrough: A carver is a dining chair with arms, traditionally used by whoever carves the meat.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a sculptor and an armchair at the head of the table, so the sculptor sits in his namesake.

clue.text: Inscription from scripture

indicators.note: from shows the letters are taken out of the inside of the next word

explanation.surface: An inscription quoted from a holy text.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for requiescat in pace, these letters are carved on gravestones, a familiar inscription.

clue.text: Very many not informed

explanation.surface: Large numbers of people kept in the dark.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means countless, and also literally not related or told to anyone.

clue.text: Suffered being related to criminal

indicators.note: criminal suggests something crooked, so the letters of the two words before it are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: A man who suffered for being a relative of a crook.
explanation.definitionFit: Suffered in the sense of put up with or allowed is a synonym of endured or permitted.

clue.text: Make out meaning of price he'd fabricated

indicators.note: fabricated means made up, so the letters of the two words before it are put together in a new order

explanation.surface: Trying to interpret a price someone invented.
explanation.definitionFit: To decode or work out the sense of something is to make out its meaning.

clue.text: Nurse carries first lady to find river

indicators.note: carries means the nurse letters hold the lady's name within them

parts.note: SRN is State Registered Nurse, an old British nursing qualification
Eve was the first woman in the Bible

explanation.surface: A nurse carrying the President's wife to reach the riverbank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first lady' suggests a president's wife, but it means Eve. The SEVERN is Britain's longest river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Severn flows from Wales through England into the Bristol Channel, an example of a river.

clue.text: Quietly drink, spilling gallons? This might be baffling!

parts.note: P stands for piano, quietly in music

indicators.note: spilling means the gallons letter is lost from the drinking word

parts.note: to guzzle is to drink greedily

explanation.surface: Someone drinking quietly yet spilling gallons, which is baffling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spilling' looks like part of the drinking picture but is the deletion signal, losing the gallons letter; the definition is the closing exclamation.
explanation.definitionFit: A conundrum or riddle is something designed to baffle whoever tries it.

clue.text: Choice of beverage when papa's promoted

indicators.note: in a down answer promoted means the papa letter is moved higher up the word

parts.note: a potion is a drink, often medicinal or magical
P is papa in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A drink is picked when Dad gets a promotion at work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'promoted' moves P up one place in POTION, past the O.
explanation.definitionFit: An option is an alternative one may select, a synonym of choice.

clue.text: Second judge initially uncertain

indicators.note: initially takes just the first letter of the judge word

parts.note: iffy means doubtful or uncertain

explanation.surface: A second judge who is unsure at first.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean a very short moment, as in 'back in a second'.

clue.text: Fine Democrat punched by expert stood opposite

indicators.note: punched by means the expert word breaks into the pair of letters, getting between them

parts.note: F is the pencil abbreviation for fine
an ace is an expert

explanation.surface: A Democrat fined and hit by a skilled fighter.
explanation.definitionFit: To face someone is to stand opposite them, so the past tense matches stood opposite.

clue.text: Piece of text soldier attached to chart

parts.note: a para is a paratrooper
a graph is a chart of data

explanation.surface: A paratrooper fastened to a map.
explanation.definitionFit: A paragraph is a section of writing, a piece of text.

clue.text: What a pity, I included assumed name

indicators.note: included means the I is put inside the regret word

parts.note: alas is an exclamation of regret

explanation.surface: Someone regrets that they gave a false name.
explanation.definitionFit: An alias is a false identity someone adopts, an assumed name.

clue.text: Stone work on nearly everything

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work

indicators.note: nearly means the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: all means everything

explanation.surface: Working on stone almost all day.
explanation.definitionFit: Opal is an iridescent gemstone, an example of a precious stone.

clue.text: Charlie's one part of frontier?

parts.note: ... Charlie was the famous crossing point on the Berlin Wall; Charlie is one such border post

explanation.surface: Wondering whether Charlie is a bit of the border.
explanation.walkthrough: Checkpoint Charlie was the Cold War crossing between East and West Berlin.
explanation.definitionFit: A border control post is a part of a frontier, and Charlie is the best known one.

clue.text: Idiot left with bottles

indicators.note: bottles means holds inside, so the two words before it contain the letters

explanation.surface: A fool left holding the bottles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bottles' looks like a noun, but it is a verb meaning contains.
explanation.definitionFit: A twit is a silly or foolish person, a synonym of idiot.

clue.text: Train that may be held up by attendant

definitions.text: Train that may be held up by attendant

parts.words: Train that may be held up by attendant
parts.note: suggests a railway train delayed by staff, but means the long trail of a wedding dress carried by a bridesmaid

explanation.surface: A train delayed by a member of its staff.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is the adjective in 'bridal train', the trailing fabric of a wedding dress.
explanation.definitionFit: A wedding dress's long trailing train is carried behind the bride by her bridesmaids.

clue.text: Second nuclear weapon is very loud

parts.note: Trident is the British submarine-launched nuclear missile system

explanation.surface: A second nuclear weapon would make a deafening noise.
explanation.definitionFit: A strident sound is harsh and loud, close to very loud.
